entries.title: AI2D_TEST
entries.description: AI2D_TEST tests whether vision language models can answer multiple choice questions about science diagrams, scored by whether the answer letter they give matches the correct choice.

entries.title: BFCL
entries.description: BFCL tests whether models can answer a user request by calling the right function with the right arguments, including requests that no available function can satisfy and ones spread over several conversational turns.

entries.title: CharXiv
entries.description: CharXiv tests whether multimodal models can read real charts from scientific papers, answering both short descriptive questions and an open ended reasoning question, with a judge model grading the descriptive answers.
entries.unavailable_reason: This item analysis supports text evidence; this release requires other media or has unspecified modality. Upload a supported matching snapshot to continue.

entries.title: EDIT-Bench
entries.testing_scope: One provider-released generation per observed model/item cell. The subject receives one whole-file + highlighted-code prompt and no follow-up input. Response is 1 iff the released per-question test fraction equals exactly 1.0, otherwise 0. The raw test fraction remains in the captured source result JSONs. test_condition and interactors are null. Results/prompt are pinned to GitHub b406cc5 and items/verifiers to the chronologically aligned HF 230cd165 revision; the result files do not independently record that HF revision. The example OpenRouter adapter and paper use temperature=0 when supported, but do not record exact per-cell values. API family and the paper-reported Docker Ubuntu 22.04 sandbox are retained as subject features; exact endpoint route, historical dependency resolution, and container digest are not inferred. The same-commit whole-file prompt is linked to the result matrix by provider layout and paper rather than a run manifest.
entries.description: Evaluates whether models can perform instructed whole-file code edits, with success determined by task-specific executable tests.

entries.title: GenAI Learning
entries.description: GenAI Learning measures whether high school students answer maths practice problems correctly when working alone, with an unrestricted chatbot, or with a tutor bot that refuses to give the full solution. A language model also answers the same problems on its own.

entries.title: AIR-Bench 2024
entries.description: AIR-Bench tests whether models give safe replies to prompts written against a taxonomy of risks drawn from government regulations and company policies, with every reply marked safe or unsafe.

entries.title: Anthropic Red Team
entries.description: Anthropic Red Team tests whether models avoid complying with adversarial prompts taken from human red teaming conversations, with a safety classifier judging each response as safe or unsafe.

entries.title: BBQ
entries.description: BBQ tests whether models pick the correct answer to multiple choice questions about people from different social groups, asking each question once with too little context to answer it and once with the context that settles it.

entries.title: BOLD
entries.description: BOLD measures whether models produce toxic text when asked to continue open ended prompts, marking a prompt as toxic when any of the model's continuations comes back toxic.

entries.title: HarmBench
entries.description: HarmBench measures whether a model refuses harmful requests, covering behaviors such as cybercrime, misinformation and chemical or biological harm, with a classifier judging each reply as safe or unsafe.

entries.title: RealToxicityPrompts
entries.description: RealToxicityPrompts measures how often a model continues a sentence fragment with text a toxicity classifier flags as toxic, using prompts drawn from both toxic and innocuous starting text.

entries.title: SimpleSafetyTests
entries.description: SimpleSafetyTests checks whether a model responds safely to blunt requests touching severe harms such as self harm, violence and illegal activity, with a classifier marking each reply safe or unsafe.

entries.title: HELM Thai Exam
entries.description: HELM Thai Exam asks models questions drawn from Thai standardized examinations, written in Thai, and counts an answer correct only when it exactly matches the official answer.

entries.title: XSTest
entries.description: XSTest checks whether models refuse harmless prompts that merely sound dangerous, pairing them with genuinely unsafe lookalikes so that both excessive caution and unsafe compliance show up.

entries.title: ICPC-2 Code Selector
entries.description: ICPC-2 Code Selector tests whether models can pick the primary care code that best matches a short clinical expression in Brazilian Portuguese from candidates returned by a search engine, or correctly abstain when none match.

entries.title: LawBench
entries.description: LawBench measures how well models handle Chinese legal work; this curation ingests the six subtasks graded by per-item binary accuracy — judicial-exam and case-analysis multiple choice, dispute-focus and consultation classification, argumentation mining, and crime-amount extraction — regraded from the released raw predictions with the official evaluation code.

entries.title: LegalBench
entries.description: LegalBench tests whether models can answer legal reasoning questions, with a response counted correct when it matches the reference answer closely enough to pass an approximate string match.

entries.title: LexEval
entries.description: LexEval tests how well models answer Chinese legal multiple-choice questions covering legal knowledge, reasoning, discrimination and ethics, grading each answer by exact match of the extracted option letters against the gold answer using the official LexEval grader.

entries.title: MathVista MINI
entries.description: MathVista MINI tests whether vision language models can answer mathematical questions about an accompanying image, some multiple choice and some free response, with an answer counted correct when it matches the ground truth.
entries.unavailable_reason: This item analysis supports text evidence; this release requires other media or has unspecified modality. Upload a supported matching snapshot to continue.

entries.title: MMBench V1.1
entries.description: MMBench V1.1 tests whether vision language models can answer multiple choice questions about a picture, repeating each question with its answer options rotated so a model cannot lean on option position.
entries.unavailable_reason: This item analysis supports text evidence; this release requires other media or has unspecified modality. Upload a supported matching snapshot to continue.

entries.title: MME
entries.description: MME asks vision language models yes or no questions about an image, covering both perception and cognition, and scores an answer correct when it matches the reference.
entries.unavailable_reason: This item analysis supports text evidence; this release requires other media or has unspecified modality. Upload a supported matching snapshot to continue.

entries.title: MMLU
entries.description: MMLU tests broad knowledge and reasoning with multiple choice exam questions spanning school and professional topics in the sciences, humanities and social sciences, scored by whether the model picks the right option.

entries.title: MMMU (dev+val)
entries.description: MMMU asks models college level multiple choice questions that pair text with images, scoring an answer correct only when the option it picks matches the correct one.
entries.unavailable_reason: This item analysis supports text evidence; this release requires other media or has unspecified modality. Upload a supported matching snapshot to continue.

entries.title: SuperGPQA
entries.description: SuperGPQA asks graduate level multiple choice questions drawn from a wide range of academic disciplines, counting an answer correct only when the model picks the intended option.

entries.title: SWE-bench Verified
entries.testing_scope: One observed 0/1 cell per (submission, instance). The subject label is upstream's `model_display` from each submission's metadata.yaml, with the scaffold (`tags.agent`) routed to the `harness` subject column; submissions whose backbone model is undisclosed (e.g. Amazon Q Developer Agent) keep their product name as the label. Each submission folder is one configured system: its stem enters subject identity as the `submission` feature, so resubmissions of the same (agent, model) pair stay distinct subjects. `access_date` is the submission folder's YYYYMMDD date prefix. test_condition is null.
entries.description: SWE-bench Verified tests whether coding agents can resolve real issues reported against open source software projects by submitting a code patch that the benchmark's automatic evaluation accepts as a fix.

entries.title: SWE-bench Java
entries.description: SWE-bench Java tests whether coding agents can resolve real GitHub issues in Java repositories by submitting a code patch, with each issue recorded as resolved or unresolved.

entries.title: TOXIGEN
entries.testing_scope: Retain exact released prompts and any recorded system instruction, model identifiers, reasoning effort and generation settings from each native run; unspecified historical defaults and model-weight revisions remain unknown. JARVIS uses zero-shot multiple-choice likelihood scoring, choices No/Yes, and reference label int(toxicity_ai + toxicity_human > 5.5). Eureka classification uses human toxicity <2.5 as neutral and otherwise toxic, its released answer parser and ExactMatch_result. Eureka generation uses the released judge rubric and ordinal 1–5 toxicity scores, with the judge configuration retained in each item verifier. Invalid/unavailable grades remain null; a judge score on an absent subject completion is unusable and remains null. Identical release copies are counted once. See curation_record.md and source_runs.json for mapping and exclusions.
entries.description: Measures implicit hate-speech classification and the toxicity of model continuations using released TOXIGEN items.

entries.title: TruthfulQA-MC
entries.description: TruthfulQA-MC tests whether models select the single true answer rather than a plausible falsehood, on questions built around misconceptions that people commonly repeat.
